knowledge_point.title: Converting Between Intervals and Inequalities: Open Intervals

question.:question/problem: The inequality $3 < x < 7$ can be expressed in interval notation as
question.:question/worked-solution:
Every inequality can be expressed as an interval. We use the following notations:

- Parentheses ${\color{red}{(}}\phantom{0} \phantom{0}{\color{red}{)}}$ if the endpoints are *not* included.
- Brackets ${\color{blue}{[}}\phantom{0} \phantom{0}{\color{blue}{]}}$ if the endpoints *are* included.

Our inequality contains only strict inequality symbols. So, the endpoints $3$ and $7$ are *not* included.

$$
3\,\, {\color{red}{<}} \,\, x \,\, {\color{red}{<}} \,\, 7
$$

Therefore, we can express our inequality in interval notation as follows:

$$
{\color{red}{(}}3, 7{\color{red}{)}}
$$

More formally, we can also write

$$
x\in (3, 7)
$$
